result.answer:
## Answer: Yes — you must pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again for this second claim.

**Why:** The fee-waiver rule (Claims FAQ, "Fee waivers" section) states:

> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12‑month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee... The waiver counts approved claims only. Refused, withdrawn and pending claims do not count toward the two-claim threshold."

At the moment you lodge this second claim, you have only **one** approved claim (the March incident) — the second claim is still pending assessment, so it doesn't yet count toward the "two or more approved claims" threshold. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement based on your approved-claims history at that time, and right now that history shows only one approved claim.

So:
- This second claim (for the incident three weeks ago) will require payment of the ¥12,000 assessment fee, per the general rule on the **Fee Schedule** page: *"The claim assessment fee is ¥12,000, payable when the claim is lodged."*
- However, **if this second claim is approved**, you will then have two approved claims from separate incidents within a rolling 12-month period. Any *further* claim you file within that same 12-month window would automatically qualify for the fee waiver — no separate application needed.
- Also worth noting from the Fee Schedule: if the final award on this second claim exceeds ¥1,000,000, the ¥12,000 fee you pay now would be refunded in full anyway, regardless of waiver status.

**Sources:** `/claims/fees/` (Fee Schedule) and `/claims/faq/` (Claims FAQ, "Fee waivers" section).

normalisations: A field value counts if it CONTAINS the expected value — "Zone 4" satisfies "4".
A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Each one existed because a check had already scored an answer wrongly, and the last of them changed a finding that had already been handed over. They are listed so a reader can judge the instrument, including its history.

Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
